1.Nf3 d5 2.c4 e6.name: English Opening: Agincourt Defence
1.Nf3 d5 2.c4 e6.background: The same position arises from 1.c4 e6 2.Nf3 d5, the Agincourt Defence of the English Opening, in which 1...e6 prepares a supported ...d5, comparable to the French Defence. In the Réti move order, 2...e6 and 2...c6 both transpose to the English Opening.

1.Nf3 d5 2.c4 e6 3.g3.strategy: Fianchettoes the king's bishop, which will press on the centre and the queenside along its long diagonal; for now the knight on f3 stands in its way. White builds a flexible, patient set-up with a safe king and decides later whether to take the centre with the d-pawn.

1.Nf3 d5 2.c4 e6 3.b3.strategy: Supports the c4-pawn, so that ...dxc4 gains nothing, and prepares the queen's bishop for the long diagonal. White aims at the centre from a distance, but the king's bishop is still undeveloped and Black has time to set up a solid centre.

1.Nf3 d5 2.c4 e6 3.b3 Nf6.strategy: Develops with a purpose: the knight guards d5 and eyes e4, so Black holds the centre with pieces as well as pawns. It also prepares castling and leaves Black free to decide how to meet White's queenside bishop.

1.Nf3 d5 2.c4 e6 3.g3 Nf6.name: English Opening: Neo-Catalan
1.Nf3 d5 2.c4 e6 3.g3 Nf6.strategy: The natural developing move: the knight guards d5, eyes e4 and lets Black castle soon. Black commits to nothing yet and leaves White to decide whether the game becomes a slow build-up or a central advance.

1.Nf3 d5 2.c4 e6 3.g3 b6.strategy: Prepares to fianchetto the queen's bishop, mirroring White's idea; from b7 it defends d5, so Black holds the centre with a piece. The cost is slower development, since the king's knight stays at home for the moment.

1.Nf3 d5 2.c4 e6 3.g3 c5.strategy: Challenges the centre at once and fights for the d4 square. Black wants active play, but d5 now has one pawn fewer behind it: after cxd5 Black must recapture and live with a more open centre.
1.Nf3 d5 2.c4 e6 3.g3 c5.name: English Opening: Agincourt Defence, Catalan Defence

1.Nf3 d5 2.c4 e6 3.g3 c6.strategy: Supports d5 with a pawn, so the c4-pawn can hardly pressure it and Black keeps a sturdy centre. Development is slower: the knight loses the c6 square, and the c8-bishop stays shut in behind the e6-pawn until Black frees it.
1.Nf3 d5 2.c4 e6 3.g3 c6.name: English Opening: Agincourt Defence, Kurajica Defence

1.Nf3 d5 2.c4 e6 3.b3 Nf6 4.Bb2.strategy: Completes the fianchetto: the bishop now bears on the f6-knight and the centre along the long diagonal, pressure from a distance rather than with a pawn. White keeps the d-pawn flexible, since an early d4 would put a pawn on the bishop's own diagonal.

1.Nf3 d5 2.c4 e6 3.b3 Nf6 4.Bb2 c5.strategy: Challenges the centre at once and takes the d4 square away from White before a pawn can settle there. Black chooses active play over the compact set-up and accepts that exchanges in the centre may leave a pair of central pawns to look after.

1.Nf3 d5 2.c4 e6 3.b3 Nf6 4.Bb2 Be7.strategy: A compact, safe choice: the bishop clears the way to castling and the d5-e6 pawn chain stays intact. Black prefers solidity to activity and leaves the fight for the centre for later, at the price of a c8-bishop that stays shut in behind the e6-pawn.

1.Nf3 d5 2.c4 e6 3.b3 Nf6 4.Bb2 Be7 5.e3.strategy: Opens the f1-bishop and covers d4, so White can castle and still choose later how to meet Black's centre. A solid, unambitious move that plays for a sound position rather than an early initiative.

1.Nf3 d5 2.c4 e6 3.b3 Nf6 4.Bb2 Be7 5.e3.name: English Opening: Agincourt Defence
1.Nf3 d5 2.c4 e6 3.b3 Nf6 4.Bb2 Be7 5.e3.strategy: Gets the king to safety and the rook into play, which completes Black's kingside development. The structure is sound and nothing is weakened, but White keeps the choice of when and how to open the centre.

1.Nf3 d5 2.c4 e6 3.b3 Nf6 4.Bb2 Be7 5.e3.name: English Opening: Agincourt Defence
1.Nf3 d5 2.c4 e6 3.b3 Nf6 4.Bb2 Be7 5.e3.strategy: Takes the centre with a pawn after preparing it with pieces. White gains space and a grip on e5 and c5, and the b2-bishop supports d4 from behind; the price is that the bishop's own diagonal is half closed and Black can challenge the pawn.

Answers White's fianchetto with one of its own, giving the queen's bishop an active diagonal to fight for the centre instead of leaving it behind the e6-pawn. Black must keep d5 well defended against the c4-pawn and the pieces behind it.

1.Nf3 d5 2.c4 e6 3.b3 Nf6 4.Bb2 c5 5.e3.name: English Opening: Agincourt Defence, Wimpy System
1.Nf3 d5 2.c4 e6 3.b3 Nf6 4.Bb2 c5 5.e3.strategy: Modest and solid: it opens the f1-bishop and covers d4, without blocking the b2-bishop's diagonal. White gives up the central pawn break for now, so Black can take the initiative with a free hand in the centre.

1.Nf3 d5 2.c4 e6 3.g3 b6 4.Bg2.strategy: Brings the bishop out and clears the way to castling. It sits behind its own knight for now, but will press down the long diagonal as soon as the knight moves.

1.Nf3 d5 2.c4 e6 3.g3 b6 4.Bg2 Bb7.strategy: Puts the bishop on the long diagonal, where it defends the d5-pawn, so Black can meet pressure on the centre with pieces. The d5-pawn blocks the bishop for now, which keeps Black's game a little passive.

1.Nf3 d5 2.c4 e6 3.g3 b6 4.Bg2 Bb7 5.O-O.name: English Opening: Agincourt Defence, Catalan Defence
1.Nf3 d5 2.c4 e6 3.g3 b6 4.Bg2 Bb7 5.O-O.strategy: Completes the kingside set-up: the king is safe behind the fianchettoed bishop and the rook is ready to back a later central advance. White plays for a long positional game against a Black centre that has no pawn break ready.

1.Nf3 d5 2.c4 e6 3.g3 Nf6 4.Bg2.strategy: Completes the fianchetto and prepares castling. The c4-pawn already challenges d5, and once the f3-knight moves the bishop adds to that pressure down the long diagonal. White plays for slow, lasting pressure on Black's centre and queenside.

1.Nf3 d5 2.c4 e6 3.g3 Nf6 4.Bg2 Be7.name: English Opening: Neo-Catalan Declined
1.Nf3 d5 2.c4 e6 3.g3 Nf6 4.Bg2 Be7.strategy: Solid and flexible: Black prepares to castle and keeps d5 firmly held. There is no commitment in the centre; Black waits for White to show a plan and accepts that White keeps a slightly freer game.

1.Nf3 d5 2.c4 e6 3.g3 Nf6 4.Bg2 c5.strategy: Strikes at the centre at once instead of supporting d5 with a pawn. With the knight already on f6 Black can recapture on d5 either way after cxd5, which gives an open, active game in which the central pawns need looking after.

1.Nf3 d5 2.c4 e6 3.g3 Nf6 4.Bg2 dxc4.name: English Opening: Agincourt Defence, Catalan Defence Accepted
1.Nf3 d5 2.c4 e6 3.g3 Nf6 4.Bg2 dxc4.strategy: Takes the pawn and frees d5, so the g2-bishop will get the whole long diagonal once the knight moves. White can regain the pawn soon, among other ways with the check Qa4+, so Black gets only a short-lived extra pawn and must complete development with care.

1.Nf3 d5 2.c4 e6 3.g3 Nf6 4.Bg2 c6.name: English Opening: Agincourt Defence, Catalan Defence, Semi-Slav Defence
1.Nf3 d5 2.c4 e6 3.g3 Nf6 4.Bg2 c6.strategy: Supports d5 with a pawn and keeps the option of taking on c4 or holding the centre. Development is slower, as the c8-bishop is shut in behind e6, but the pawn structure is hard to break down.

1.Nf3 d5 2.c4 e6 3.g3 Nf6 4.Bg2 b6.strategy: Mirrors White's fianchetto, but d5 is already under pressure from the c4-pawn and the bishop on b7 would be shut in behind that pawn. Playable, though Black gets less from it than from the more usual ways of supporting the centre.

1.Nf3 d5 2.c4 e6 3.g3 Nf6 4.Bg2 Bd6.name: English Opening: Agincourt Defence, Bogoljubow Defence
1.Nf3 d5 2.c4 e6 3.g3 Nf6 4.Bg2 Bd6.strategy: An offbeat alternative to the usual bishop development: it aims at the kingside and supports a later ...e5, but it is less flexible than the retreat to e7 and blocks the d-file, so Black has fewer ways to react to White's pressure on the centre.

1.Nf3 d5 2.c4 e6 3.g3 Nf6 4.Bg2 b6 5.O-O.name: King's Indian Attack: Yugoslav Variation
1.Nf3 d5 2.c4 e6 3.g3 Nf6 4.Bg2 b6 5.O-O.strategy: Castles at once: the king is safe and White needs no more than normal development to keep the pressure on Black's centre. Black's fianchetto has not yet taken a stand against the c4-d5 tension, so White can choose the moment to act.

1.Nf3 d5 2.c4 e6 3.g3 Nf6 4.Bg2 Be7 5.O-.name: English Opening: Agincourt Defence, Neo-Catalan Declined
1.Nf3 d5 2.c4 e6 3.g3 Nf6 4.Bg2 Be7 5.O-.strategy: Castles first and keeps a central advance and a second fianchetto in reserve. White waits to see how Black sets up and commits to a plan only then.

1.Nf3 d5 2.c4 e6 3.g3 Nf6 4.Bg2 Be7 5.d4.name: Catalan Opening: Closed
1.Nf3 d5 2.c4 e6 3.g3 Nf6 4.Bg2 Be7 5.d4.background: The Catalan is named for Catalonia: the organisers of the Barcelona tournament of 1929 asked Savielly Tartakower to create a new variation in homage to Catalonia's chess history.
1.Nf3 d5 2.c4 e6 3.g3 Nf6 4.Bg2 Be7 5.d4.strategy: Occupies the centre with a pawn and sets the c4-d4 pair against Black's d5-e6 structure. White plays for a small, lasting space advantage and queenside pressure; in return the c4-pawn can become a target if Black takes it.

1.Nf3 d5 2.c4 e6 3.g3 Nf6 4.Bg2 Be7 5.b3.name: English Opening: Agincourt Defence, Neo-Catalan Declined, Early b3
1.Nf3 d5 2.c4 e6 3.g3 Nf6 4.Bg2 Be7 5.b3.strategy: Chooses the double fianchetto: both bishops will aim at the centre and the queenside from a distance, and the c4-pawn is firmly protected. The central pawn advance is postponed, so Black gets time to claim a share of the centre.

1.Nf3 d5 2.c4 e6 3.g3 Nf6 4.Bg2 Be7 5.b3.name: English Opening: Agincourt Defence, Neo-Catalan Declined, Early b3
1.Nf3 d5 2.c4 e6 3.g3 Nf6 4.Bg2 Be7 5.b3.strategy: Mirrors White's set-up: the queen's bishop goes to the long diagonal to fight for the centre, and both sides now play with a double fianchetto. Black frees the c8-bishop from behind the e6-pawn but still has no central pawn break.

1.Nf3 d5 2.c4 e6 3.g3 Nf6 4.Bg2 Be7 5.b3.name: English Opening: Agincourt Defence, Neo-Catalan Declined, Early b3
1.Nf3 d5 2.c4 e6 3.g3 Nf6 4.Bg2 Be7 5.b3.strategy: Challenges the centre instead of copying White's set-up, and takes d4 away from the pieces White is preparing. Black accepts an open game, in which the d5-pawn loses one of its pawn defenders if White takes on d5.

1.Nf3 d5 2.c4 e6 3.g3 Nf6 4.Bg2 Be7 5.d4.strategy: Gets the king to safety before the tension in the centre is resolved, and keeps the sturdy d5-e6 pawn chain. Black leaves the fight for the centre until White shows what the queenside pressure will look like.

1.Nf3 d5 2.c4 e6 3.g3 Nf6 4.Bg2 Be7 5.O-.strategy: Finishes the kingside development and gets the king safe before Black commits in the centre. The compact structure stays intact and Black waits for White to show a plan, with the c8-bishop still the shut-in piece.
Challenges the centre before castling: the c-pawn hits d4, and the exchange on d5 would open lines for Black's pieces. Black seeks active counterplay and accepts a small delay in castling.

1.Nf3 d5 2.c4 e6 3.g3 Nf6 4.Bg2 Be7 5.d4.strategy: Completes the kingside set-up: the king is safe behind the fianchettoed bishop and the rook is ready for the centre. White now plays for pressure on the queenside and on the c4-d5 tension, against a Black position that is solid but somewhat cramped.

1.Nf3 d5 2.c4 e6 3.g3 Nf6 4.Bg2 Be7 5.d4.name: Catalan Opening: Open Defence, Classical Line
1.Nf3 d5 2.c4 e6 3.g3 Nf6 4.Bg2 Be7 5.d4.strategy: Takes the pawn and gives White the open long diagonal for the bishop. White can win the pawn back, so Black has to use the time to free the queenside and finish development; the c4-pawn is more a loan than a gain.

1.Nf3 d5 2.c4 e6 3.g3 Nf6 4.Bg2 Be7 5.d4.name: Catalan Opening: Closed
1.Nf3 d5 2.c4 e6 3.g3 Nf6 4.Bg2 Be7 5.d4.strategy: Solid: the pawn adds to the defence of d5 and shuts the long diagonal for good. Black keeps a compact position that is hard to attack, though the c8-bishop is still shut in and the game stays cramped for a while.

1.Nf3 d5 2.c4 e6 3.g3 Nf6 4.Bg2 Be7 5.d4.name: Catalan Opening: Closed
1.Nf3 d5 2.c4 e6 3.g3 Nf6 4.Bg2 Be7 5.d4.strategy: Develops the last knight and keeps d5 held, leaving ...dxc4 for later, while preparing a central pawn break. The knight blocks the c8-bishop's diagonal for now, so Black is still short of space.

1.Nf3 d5 2.c4 e6 3.g3 Nf6 4.Bg2 Be7 5.O-.strategy: Removes the tension in the centre at once and makes Black recapture, so the centre opens. White's c-file is now half open against the c5-pawn, which becomes the target.

Recaptures with a piece, keeping Black's pawn structure intact and putting a knight in the centre. The knight can be challenged, the c8-bishop is still shut in behind e6, and Black must watch the c5-pawn on the half-open c-file.

1.Nf3 d5 2.c4 e6 3.g3 Nf6 4.Bg2 Be7 5.O-.name: English Opening: Agincourt Defence, Neo-Catalan Declined
1.Nf3 d5 2.c4 e6 3.g3 Nf6 4.Bg2 Be7 5.O-.strategy: Prepares the double fianchetto after castling: both bishops will aim at the centre and the c4-pawn is supported, so Black cannot win it. White avoids committing the d-pawn and keeps the position flexible, a slower but safe plan.

1.Nf3 d5 2.c4 e6 3.g3 Nf6 4.Bg2 Be7 5.O-.name: English Opening: Agincourt Defence, Neo-Catalan Declined
1.Nf3 d5 2.c4 e6 3.g3 Nf6 4.Bg2 Be7 5.O-.strategy: Strikes at d4 at once, so White cannot easily build a centre there, and keeps the c-pawn active instead of tucking it away on c6. Black accepts a more open, more dynamic game in which the d5-pawn needs watching but the pieces have room.

Reinforces d5 with a pawn and keeps the structure compact and hard to attack. The price is passivity: the c8-bishop stays shut in behind the chain, so Black has a very safe position but little counterplay until it is freed.

1.Nf3 d5 2.c4 e6 3.g3 Nf6 4.Bg2 c5 5.b3.strategy: Protects the c4-pawn and prepares the queen's bishop for the long diagonal. White does not rush to take the centre; the cost is a slower game, in which Black's c-pawn has already taken d4 under control.
Develops the knight and adds to the pressure on d4, so Black fights for the centre with pawns and pieces alike. A natural, flexible choice that keeps the c-pawn well supported.
Gets the king safe and finishes the kingside set-up. White's plan is a long, patient game: the queen's bishop will come to b2 and the pieces aim at the centre from the flanks rather than occupy it.

1.Nf3 d5 2.c4 e6 3.g3 Nf6 4.Bg2 c5 5.b3.name: English Opening: Agincourt Defence, Tarrasch Defence
1.Nf3 d5 2.c4 e6 3.g3 Nf6 4.Bg2 c5 5.b3.strategy: Defends the c5-pawn, which the knight on c6 does not, and prepares castling. Black's development is complete enough to meet White's flank pressure, at the price of a modest, reactive position.

1.Nf3 d5 2.c4 e6 3.g3 Nf6 4.Bg2 c6 5.b3.strategy: Protects the c4-pawn and prepares the queen's bishop for the long diagonal, keeping the pawn structure flexible instead of building a pawn centre at once. White keeps c4 solid and aims at the centre from a distance.

Develops the bishop to its natural square and prepares castling, while the pawns on c6, d5 and e6 stay as they are. Black chooses a solid, slightly passive set-up and waits for White to show a plan; the c8-bishop still has to be freed later.

1.Nf3 d5 2.c4 e6 3.g3 Nf6 4.Bg2 c6 5.b3.name: Réti Opening: Anglo-Slav Variation
1.Nf3 d5 2.c4 e6 3.g3 Nf6 4.Bg2 c6 5.b3.strategy: Completes the double fianchetto: the bishop looks along the long diagonal at the f6 knight and the e5 square, and White controls the centre with pieces from a distance instead of occupying it with pawns. A slow, manoeuvring game follows, in which neither side has much to attack at first.
